purpose: Adds guarded WP 6.9+ pluggable overrides for the four salted-cache functions to the Redis object-cache drop-in, plus a PHPUnit test file.
riskRationale: The implementation itself is functionally self-consistent and matches core's wrapper-at-stable-key format, but the PR description materially misrepresents the change (claims salt-in-key that the code does not implement), the stated performance goal is not achieved, and there is a real risk the overrides are never invoked because wp_cache_supports() does not advertise the salted-cache feature.

text: The four overrides are well-structured: correctly guarded with if ( ! function_exists() ), use core's (unswapped) signatures, normalize array salts with implode(':'), and remap get/set_multiple results, matching the reference cache-compat.php layout. However the code implements the wrapper-at-stable-key strategy while the PR description claims salt-in-key plus removal of the wrapper encode/decode, so the change does not deliver the claimed performance benefit and the narrative, docblocks, and open threads are inconsistent.

reasoning: The code is internally correct but does not match the PR description's stated strategy or performance claim, and it may be dead code if wp_cache_supports('cache_salted') is never enabled. The description must be corrected (or the implementation re-scoped) and core routing confirmed before merge.

message: Signatures are correct: getters use ($cache_key, $group, $salt) and setters use ($cache_key, $data, $group, $salt, $expire) — deliberately not the swapped order suggested in the issue, which would have broken every call site. Array salts are normalized identically on both setter and getter via implode(':',$salt), keeping writes/reads consistent.
All four functions are wrapped in if (!function_exists()) guards, correctly mirroring WP core's pluggable pattern, so WP < 6.9 sites using cache-compat.php are unaffected.

The test class includes valuable behavioral coverage beyond simple mock assertions: round-trip with same salt, miss on different salt, overwrite-on-same-stable-key (proves bounded memory), exact stored wrapper format parity, unsalted write_cache_delete invalidation, get/set_multiple remapping, and array-salt normalization ordering.

The implementation contradicts the PR description. The description states the drop-in 'embeds the salt directly into the Redis key ... storing raw data, eliminating core's wrapper-array (data/salt) encode/decode + PHP salt comparison on every read' by passing $cache_key.':'.$salt. Instead the code stores a wrapper array array('data'=>..., 'salt'=>...) at the stable key and still performs the PHP salt comparison on every read (lines 936-1036) — identical to WP core's cache-compat.php. The stated performance optimization and the 'salt-in-key' (Option A) approach are not implemented; the override duplicates core's fallback exactly, provides no measurable benefit, and adds future drift risk. The PR title/narrative and the three unresolved review threads (written against a salt-in-key version) are stale and misleading.
suggestion: Rewrite the PR description to reflect reality: the change adopts core's wrapper-at-stable-key format (which resolves the memory concern but yields no perf gain identical to cache-compat). Decide and state whether the intent is (a) drop these redundant overrides entirely (core's cache-compat already handles them via wp_cache_get/set), or (b) keep them solely for WP<6.9 robustness — and update the stale open threads accordingly.

message: wp_cache_supports() returns false for every feature other than flush_group/get_multiple/set_multiple/delete_multiple, so it does not advertise support for salted caching. If WP core gates use of the salted API behind wp_cache_supports('cache_salted'), the four new override functions (lines 919-1036) will never be called and this entire PR becomes dead code — core would fall back to the non-salted path regardless. This must be confirmed against WP 6.9 core; without ensuring its invocation, the change has no effect.
suggestion: Verify WP 6.9 core's routing for salted caching. If the overrides are meant to take effect, advertise support in wp_cache_supports() by adding a 'cache_salted' case (and confirm the drop-in's WP_Object_Cache can back it); if core never consults this for the drop-in, the overrides are redundant with cache-compat.php and should be removed.

message: This test file will never execute under the current harness. phpunit.xml.dist points the testsuite at tests/php with no explicit testSuffix, so PHPUnit 11's default suffix 'Test.php' compared against 'class-object-cache-test.php' discovers zero tests (verified: vendor/bin/phpunit reports 'No tests executed!'). The pre-existing class-*-test.php files have the same issue, but adding a new test that is never run gives false confidence; the PR's stated verification ('npm test' Jest 18 suites + composer lint) does not include running these PHP tests.
suggestion: Wire the PHP suite into CI and ensure discovery (rename files to *Test.php or set <testSuiteFileFilter>/suffix), then run composer test as part of verification; additionally call BrainMock tearDown() (e.g. use the existing WPPO_Test_Bootstrap trait's tearDown) to avoid leaking BrainMonkey global state between tests.
